# Quick Reference: Excel, SQL, and DAX {#sec-appendix-reference}

This appendix gathers the functions and commands the book teaches, so that you can look one up without searching for the chapter that introduced it. It lists only what the chapters use, grouped by tool and by purpose, and each entry names the chapter that explains it, which is where to find an example on the Charles River data. Arguments have short placeholder names, and optional arguments are left out unless the book uses them. The last section sets the three tools side by side, with the same calculations in Excel, SQL, and DAX.


## Excel

The Excel chapters of Part II teach these functions, and a few appear earlier, in the tutorials of Part I. Every formula begins with an equals sign, which the tables leave out. Microsoft's alphabetical list of Excel functions describes each one in full (Microsoft, n.d.).

| Function | What it does | Chapter |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|:---------|
| `XLOOKUP(key, keys, results)` | Finds a key in one column and returns the value beside it, with an exact match by default; a fourth argument supplies a value when the key is not found | 2, 5 |
| `VLOOKUP(key, range, n, FALSE)` | Finds a key in the first column of a range and returns the value in its nth column | 5 |
| `INDEX(range, MATCH(...))` | MATCH, with 0 as its last argument, finds the position of a key, and INDEX returns the value at that position | 5 |
| `IF(test, if_true, if_false)` | One of two values, depending on a test | 2, 5 |
| `IFS(test1, value1, ...)` | The value paired with the first true test | 5 |
| `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` | TRUE if every test is true, if at least one is, or if the test is false | 5 |
| `IFERROR(value, if_error)` | The value, or a substitute when the value is an error | 5 |

## Power Query

Power Query is the same editor in Excel, where Part II uses it, and in Power BI, where Part IV does. Its commands record steps that run again at every refresh, and a custom column holds a formula in M, Power Query's language. M is case-sensitive, and its text functions count characters from 0, where Excel and SQL count from 1. Microsoft's M function reference describes each function (Microsoft, 2025).

| Command | What it does | Chapter |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|:---------|
| Get Data | Connects to a source; for CharlesRiver.xlsx, choose its Tables in the Navigator | 4, 13 |
| Choose Columns | Keeps only the columns you select, as the step Removed Other Columns | 4 |
| A column's filter | Keeps the rows that pass it, before the data load | 4 |
| Data type, Replace current | Sets a column's type in the Changed Type step itself; check the types, because Power Query sets each column's type from its first 200 rows | 4, 13 |
| Merge Queries | Adds columns from another query by matching a key; expand them without the column-name prefix | 5 |
| Join kind | Left outer keeps every row of the first query; left anti keeps only its rows that have no match | 5 |
| Group By | Totals or counts rows by one or more columns; Advanced allows more than one column or total | 6 |
| Custom Column | Adds a column computed by an M formula | 5 |
| Conditional Column | Adds a column from if-then rules, without writing M | 5 |
| Replace Values | Replaces one value with another in a column | 8 |
| Append Queries | Stacks the rows of two or more queries that have the same columns | 16 |
| Unpivot Only Selected Columns | Turns the chosen columns into rows of attribute and value | 16 |
| Enable Load | Cleared for a query that only feeds other queries | 6, 13 |
| Close & Load, Close & Apply | Loads the queries into Excel worksheets, or into the Power BI model | 4, 13 |
| Refresh All, Refresh | Runs every query again against its source | 4, 13 |
| Column quality, distribution, profile | Profile each column, on the first rows only unless profiling is set to the entire data set | 13 |

| `Date.QuarterOfYear([d])` | The quarter of a date, 1 to 4 | 5 |
| `Date.ToText([d], "yyyy-MM")` | A date as text, in a format | 13 |
| `Date.From([dt])` | The date of a date and time | 16 |
| `Date.DayOfWeek([d], Day.Monday)` | The day of the week, from 0 for Monday to 6 for Sunday | 16 |

## SQL

The SQL chapters of Part III query SQLite through DB Browser for SQLite. SQLite's documentation describes its functions and the behaviors that differ from other databases (SQLite, n.d.-a, n.d.-b, n.d.-c, n.d.-d, n.d.-e). Keywords are written in capitals, by the book's convention, and the double bar operator joins texts, so `a || ' ' || b` puts a space between a and b (Chapter 9).

| Clause | What it does | Evaluated | Chapter |
|:--------------------|:------------------------------------------------|:----------|:---------|
| `SELECT` | The columns and expressions to return; `DISTINCT` removes duplicate rows | 5th | 9 |
| `FROM`, `JOIN ... ON` | The tables, and how their rows match | 1st | 9, 10 |
| `WHERE` | Keeps the rows that meet a condition, before any grouping | 2nd | 9 |
| `GROUP BY` | One row for each value of the grouping columns | 3rd | 10 |
| `HAVING` | Keeps the groups that meet a condition | 4th | 10 |
| `ORDER BY` | Sorts the result, ascending unless `DESC` follows | 6th | 9 |
| `LIMIT n` | Returns the first n rows | 7th | 9 |

: The clauses of a query, in written order, with the step at which each is evaluated {#tbl-a-09}

Window functions are calculated after HAVING and before ORDER BY, which is why they cannot appear in WHERE or HAVING (Chapter 11).

| Construct | What it does | Chapter |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|:---------|
| `INNER JOIN t ON ...` | Only the rows that have a match in both tables | 10 |
| `LEFT JOIN t ON ...` | Every row of the first table, with NULLs where the second has no match | 10 |
| Anti-join | A LEFT JOIN followed by `WHERE key IS NULL`, which keeps the rows without a match | 10 |
| `NOT EXISTS (subquery)` | The rows for which the subquery finds nothing; unlike NOT IN, it is safe when the list holds NULLs | 10 |
| `IN (subquery)` | The rows whose value is in the list the subquery returns | 10 |
| Scalar subquery | A subquery that returns one value, used where a value is expected | 10 |
| Correlated subquery | A subquery that refers to the outer row, and runs once for each row | 10 |
| Derived table | A subquery in FROM, named with an alias | 10 |
| Self-join | A table joined to itself under two aliases | 12 |
| `WITH name AS (...)` | A common table expression: a named query that later steps read | 11 |
| `UNION ALL` | Stacks the rows of two queries that have the same columns | 12 |
| `CREATE VIEW name AS` | Saves a query in the database; run `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS` first, and `TEMP` keeps it for the session only | 11 |

: Joins, subqueries, and saved queries {#tbl-a-10}

| Function or operator | What it does | Chapter |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|:---------|
| `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` | Comparisons; `=` on text is case-sensitive | 9 |
| `BETWEEN a AND b` | Within a range, including both ends | 9 |
| `IN (a, b, c)` | Equal to any value in the list | 9 |
| `LIKE 'A%'` | Matches a pattern, in which `%` stands for any characters; not case-sensitive for the letters A to Z | 9 |
| `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL` | Has no value, or has one | 9 |
| `ROUND(x, d)` | x rounded to d decimal places; a negative d is taken as 0 | 9 |
| `ABS(x)` | x without its sign | 9 |
| `CAST(x AS type)` | x converted to INTEGER, REAL, or TEXT | 9 |
| `UPPER(x)`, `LOWER(x)` | x in capitals, or in lower case | 9 |
| `TRIM(x)` | x without spaces at either end | 9 |
| `REPLACE(x, a, b)` | x with every a replaced by b | 9 |
| `LENGTH(x)` | The number of characters in x | 9 |
| `SUBSTR(x, s, n)` | n characters of x from position s, counted from 1; without n, the rest of x | 9 |
| `COALESCE(x, y)`, `IFNULL(x, y)` | x, or y when x is NULL | 9 |
| `CASE WHEN ... THEN ... END` | The result paired with the first true condition, or the ELSE value | 11 |
| `COUNT(*)`, `COUNT(column)` | The number of rows, or of values that are not NULL | 10 |
| `COUNT(DISTINCT column)` | The number of different values | 10 |
| `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX` | Totals, averages, and extremes, skipping NULLs | 10 |
| `GROUP_CONCAT(column, sep)` | The values joined into one text | 10 |
| `strftime('%Y', d)` | A part of a date, as text: `%Y` the year, `%m` the month, `%w` the weekday | 11 |
| `date(d, modifier)` | A date moved by modifiers such as `'start of month'`, applied in order | 11 |
| `julianday(d)` | The date as a number of days, for the difference between two dates | 11 |
| `printf('%e', x)` | x as text, here in scientific notation | 12 |
| `LOG10(x)` | The base-10 logarithm of x | 12 |
| `sqlite_version()` | The version of SQLite in use; window functions need version 3.25 or later | 11 |

: Functions and operators {#tbl-a-11}

| Function or clause | What it does | Chapter |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|:---------|
| `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...)` | A sequence number within the partition, even for ties | 11 |
| `RANK()`, `DENSE_RANK()` | A rank in which ties share a number; RANK skips the numbers after a tie | 11 |
| `SUM(x) OVER (...)` | A total over the window: the whole partition, or a running or moving total; AVG, COUNT, MIN, and MAX work the same way | 11 |
| `LAG(x, n)`, `LEAD(x, n)` | The value of x n rows before, or after, the current row | 11 |
| `PARTITION BY column` | Divides the rows into groups that the window never crosses | 11 |
| `ORDER BY` inside `OVER` | Orders each partition; an aggregate's default window then runs to the current row and the rows that tie with it | 11 |
| `ROWS BETWEEN ...` | With `n PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`, the current row and the n before it; `ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING` runs from the first row | 11 |
| `WINDOW w AS (...)` | Names a window, for use as `OVER w` | 11 |

: Window functions and clauses {#tbl-a-12}

| Behavior | What it means | Chapter |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|:---------|
| Integer division | `7 / 2` returns 3; multiply one side by 1.0 for a decimal result | 9 |
| `%` | Returns the remainder, after dropping the decimals of both numbers | 9 |
| Comparisons with NULL | Never true, so test for a missing value with IS NULL | 9 |
| Sorting NULLs | NULLs come first in ascending order | 9 |
| Dates | Stored as text in the form YYYY-MM-DD, so they compare and sort correctly as text | 9 |
| Type affinity | A value is converted to the type of the column it is compared with, never between two expressions, so `SUBSTR(x, 1, 4) = 2026` finds no rows when x is text; compare with `'2026'` | 9, 11 |
| Double quotes | A double-quoted value is read as a column name, and as text only when no column has that name; write text in single quotes | 9 |
| A missing comma | Makes the next column an alias of the one before it, a logical error with no message | 9 |
| An alias in GROUP BY | Accepted by SQLite, though some databases, such as SQL Server, reject it | 10 |

: SQLite behaviors the book relies on {#tbl-a-13}


## DAX

The Power BI chapters of Part IV write DAX in measures, calculated columns, calculated tables, and queries. The book puts a space inside each parenthesis and quotes the table names Date and Item, which are reserved words (Chapter 14). Microsoft's DAX function reference describes each function (Microsoft, 2023).

| Function | What it does | Chapter |
|:---------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|:---------|
| `SUM ( column )` | Adds up a column over the rows in the filter context | 14 |
| `COUNTROWS ( table )` | The number of rows of a table | 14 |
| `DISTINCTCOUNT ( column )` | The number of different values of a column | 14 |
| `MAX ( column )`, `MIN ( column )` | The largest or smallest value | 14 |
| `DIVIDE ( a, b )` | a divided by b, or a blank when b is zero | 14 |
| `SUMX ( table, expression )` | Evaluates an expression row by row and adds the results | 14 |
| `MINX`, `MAXX` | The smallest or largest result of an expression over a table | 16 |
| `ROUND ( x, d )`, `ABS ( x )` | x rounded to d decimal places, or x without its sign | 14 |
| `LOG10 ( x )` | The base-10 logarithm of x | 16 |

## The Same Calculation in Three Tools

The chapters return to a handful of calculations in each tool. @tbl-a-19 sets them side by side, with the chapters in parentheses, so that a technique learned in one Part can be found in the others.

| Task | Excel | SQL | DAX and Power BI |
|:------------------|:-------------------------|:-------------------------|:-------------------------|
| Total under a condition | SUMIFS (4) | SUM with WHERE, or with GROUP BY (10); SUM of a CASE (11) | CALCULATE with a filter (14) |
| Count distinct values | COUNTA of UNIQUE (7) | COUNT(DISTINCT) (10) | DISTINCTCOUNT (14) |
| Bring in a value from another table | XLOOKUP, or a merge in Power Query (5) | A JOIN on the key (10) | A relationship, and RELATED row by row (14) |
| Find rows with no match | A left anti merge, or COUNTIFS against the parent table (2, 5) | An anti-join or NOT EXISTS (10) | The (Blank) row in a visual (13, 14) |
| Summarize by group | A PivotTable, or Group By in Power Query (4, 6) | GROUP BY (10) | A matrix visual, or SUMMARIZECOLUMNS in a query (13, 14) |
| Share of a total | Show Values As % of Grand Total (6) | SUM over an empty window, OVER () (11) | DIVIDE with REMOVEFILTERS (14) |
| Running total | Show Values As Running Total In (6) | SUM over a window ordered by date (11) | TOTALYTD, or the RUNNINGSUM visual calculation (14, 15) |
| Change from the previous period | Show Values As Difference From (6) | LAG (11) | DATEADD or SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, or the PREVIOUS visual calculation (14, 15) |
| Trailing twelve months | Not covered | A window of the current row and the 11 before it (11) | DATESINPERIOD over 12 months, or MOVINGAVERAGE (15) |

: The same calculations in Excel, SQL, and DAX {#tbl-a-19}
